messages.author: 4edd96ba555fea10
messages.subject: Estimating posterior modes
parts:
Hi Paul,

Is it possible to estimate posterior modes rather than means through BRMS? In particular I am interested in whether this is possible when using a gamma likelihood.

Thank you for your help.

Tim

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: Estimating posterior modes
parts:
Let's say you are interested in the posterior mode of the population-level intercept. Then you can do the follwing:

# extract posterior samples
ps <- as.matrix(fit, "^b_Intercept$")
# compute the mode
estimate_mode <- function(x) {
  # quick and dirty way to compute the mode
  d <- density(x)
  d$x[which.max(d$y)]
}
estimate_mode(ps)

Is this what you had in mind?

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Estimating posterior modes
parts:
I didn't see this post until now, but I just wanted to caution against using the posterior mode in general. The major benefit of Bayesian modeling via MCMC is that it lets you easily compute posterior expectations. Just finding the posterior mode is throwing away almost all of the useful information in the posterior distribution. If you absolutely want only a point estimate then you can take the median (which minimizes expected absolute error) or the mean (which minimizes expected squared error), but the posterior mode really has no interpretation (and is not invariant to reparameterization). 

Jonah
